messages:
Avery (oncall): alert: sudden 5xx spike from canary pool in us-west-2, paging oncall
DeployBot: ALERT | Sev2 | service=inference-api | symptom=5xx spike on canary | paged=@Avery (oncall) @Meng (sre)
Avery (oncall): oncall here, looking. Any deploys finishing in last 10m?
Priya (release): yes, automated canary promoted a minute ago. I saw a second image tag appear during the pipeline run.
Devin (platform): digging into registry: two tags (canary-2026-03-15 and release-2026-03-15) point at different digests, and there was a concurrent CI publish step. Looks like a retag race.
Meng (sre): impact: ~35% of canary pods failing with model init errors -> 500s. Frontend retries causing head-of-line issues for streaming endpoints.
Kelsey (support): getting customer tickets for failed batch embeddings from 2 enterprise tenants. Escalating to P1.
Avery (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) stop routing to new canary instances (feature flag or LB change) 2) scale down canary ASG / pool 3) rollback any pods using suspect image digest 4) audit CI publish behavior.
Priya (release): can't pause the already-completed promotion, but we can flip the routing flag `ff.inference.reroute=false`. Doing that now.
CI-Bot: DEPLOY | promotion detected | deployment/inference-api promoted canary-2026-03-15 -> replicaset/rs-canary-xyz
Priya (release): routing flag flipped -> confirm drains in progress.
Meng (sre): traffic to canary dropped to ~1.8% then 0. Errors on frontends trending down. Good.
Devin (platform): prepping rollback. We're going to pin deployment to immutable digest sha256:0a1b2c3d4e and run a controlled rollout to stable nodes.
Priya (release): applying: `kubectl -n prod set image deployment/inference-api inference-api=gcr.io/redwood/inference@sha256:0a1b2c3d4e`
Devin (platform): `kubectl rollout status deployment/inference-api -n prod` -> rollout progressing, pods becoming ready on pinned digest.
Meng (sre): metrics: 5xx rate back to baseline within ~4 minutes of flag flip + rollback. KV caches warmed on stable instances.
Avery (oncall): mitigation successful. Now root cause: CI allowed concurrent publish+retag of mutable tags. Immediate remediations and longer-term fixes needed.
Action items:
- Priya (release): hotfix CI pipeline to forbid mutable retagging; require pushes by digest or unique build id. ETA: 24h.
- Devin (platform): add registry push lock (mutex) to CI agent and disable parallel publish steps. ETA: 6h for staging, 24h for prod rollout.
- Meng (sre): add gating that prevents automatic promotion if canary health degrades during promotion window; tighten canary health checks. ETA: 3d.
- Avery (oncall): author incident summary and customer impact note. ETA: 2h.
Priya (release): opened hotfix PR: https://git.internal/redwood/ci/pulls/523 -> adds validation to block tag reuse and enforces `--digest` pushes.
Kelsey (support): notified affected customers: described mitigation (flag flip + rollback) and offered to re-run failed jobs. Scheduling follow-up calls.
Ben (pm): can we get rough numbers on failures for report?
Meng (sre): preliminary numbers: ~2.9k failed requests in a 14-minute window, about 0.14% of global traffic. Two enterprise batch jobs experienced multi-hour retries.
Avery (oncall): ok, we'll keep monitoring for 2 hours, keep incident open until CI hotfix lands in staging. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
DeployBot: INCIDENT UPDATE | status=mitigated | handler=Avery (oncall) | severity=degraded -> downgraded
Avery (oncall): I'll draft the postmortem and link follow-ups.
Priya (release): adding CI lint that fails builds which attempt to push to mutable tags.
Devin (platform): deploying registry push lock to CI staging now.
Meng (sre): adding alert to detect tag swaps/retags and concurrent pushes to same repository.
Kelsey (support): leaving notes in customer tickets, will schedule the follow-up.
Avery (oncall): incident closed for active mitigation; follow-ups tracked in linked RFC. If any regressions appear, ping this thread.
